transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-30 16:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel, Miguel Ortega, Caroline Wu (Redwood) — Rina Shah, Marcus Lee, Dana Price, Noah Park (GlimmerOps)

Summary (auto): Quick check-in ahead of renewal; GlimmerOps targets Q4 activation for EU private nodes and needs clarity on dedicated capacity uplift and KMS/HSM requirements. They want a short POC for latency and token economics.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — I'm Sofia, AE on the account, with Miguel our SE and Caroline CSM. Rina, do you want to kick off?
[00:18] Rina: Yeah, hi thanks — so overall we're happy with Redwood performance but we planned to talk renewal numbers, add EU capacity, and figure out the VPC route. Our compliance team is asking for KMS and audit log details before we sign.
[00:33] Marcus: Also from infra, latency spikes during peak hour last month were concerning — want to understand if that's Dedicated sizing, batching config, or something else.
[00:45] Miguel: Right, good callout. We did see a pattern that looks like burst packing alignment — sometimes requests from similar prefixes line up and that can cause transient spike. We have config knobs: continuous batching windows, KV cache warmers, and also can route certain routes to lower-latency Dedicated pools.
[01:10] Dana: If possible we'd like to keep user PII in EU cluster and have inference happen there. Is private onprem the only way or can VPC + region pinning work?
[01:26] Sofia: Short answer: both are possible. VPC private deployment with customer-managed networking works for residency. Onprem is for air-gapped or where you need physical isolation. There's a cost and ops tradeoff.
[01:40] Noah: Procurement question — are there minimum terms for Dedicated reserved capacity? We prefer month-to-month but recognize committed capacity lowers unit price.
[01:50] Caroline: Our Dedicated product typically offers quarterly and annual commitments. We can model a stepped commit so you ramp capacity across quarters to lower your risk. We'll include that in pricing sketches.
[02:05] Rina: Can you also send the SOC 2 and encryption docs? We need to show to legal.
[02:12] Caroline: Absolutely — I'll drop SOC2, KMS integration notes, and a VPC checklist to the shared Confluence folder after the call.
[02:20] [Speaker 1]: (mumble) sorry, yeah
[02:27] Miguel: Back to latency: if you share sample QPS and token distribution, we can simulate expected p95/p99 with a small perf harness. For the POC we'd run both hosted and dedicated variants to show latency vs cost trade-off.
[02:44] Marcus: Our median seq length is ~512 tokens for assist flows, peak bursts to 1.2k. QPS averages 35, peaking 220. Does that change the recommendation?
[02:58] Miguel: Those peaks push you to Dedicated with autoscale headroom, or a blended approach — route latency-critical routes to Dedicated, and less-critical batch to hosted. Also prefix caching can shave token compute if there are repeated contexts.
[03:15] Rina: What's the timeline if we wanted EU private pilot in November?
[03:21] Sofia: Pilot in November is tight but doable — depends on whether you want onprem hardware procurement or managed VPC in our EU region. VPC path is faster, likely 2–4 weeks for onboarding after contract; onprem is longer because of hardware and networking.
[03:38] Dana: We prefer VPC in EU first, then evaluate onprem for full sovereignty. KMS question: do you integrate with customer KMS or we have to use cloud provider keys?
[03:49] Miguel: We support customer KMS via standard key-wrap integrations and can plug into your cloud KMS or bring-your-own HSM depending on the level of assurance. If HSM is required, there are additional ops steps and lead time.
[04:05] Noah: Any blocker from procurement on the SSO/SCIM?
[04:09] Caroline: We support SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, RBAC is available. I'll include SSO flow diagrams in the doc drop.
[04:20] [00:04:20] Rina: Okay let's talk numbers — what are our options?
[04:26] Sofia: We'll prepare three sketches: 1) Hosted expansion (pay-as-you-go) — lowest ops but highest per-token unit cost; 2) Dedicated reserved capacity — best p95 latency and mid-level cost; 3) Private VPC with reserved nodes — higher ops but meets residency and KMS constraints. We'll show unit economics for your median 512 token bursts as well as peak scenarios.
[04:50] Marcus: For Dedicated, is there an SLA on p95?
[04:54] Miguel: Yes, we have SLO-backed latency tiers; for reserved Dedicated pools we guarantee throughput and have failover routing. Exact p95 SLA depends on the tier, we'll include target numbers in the offer.
[05:09] Dana: Any caveats around quantization or model variants for EU? We use some LLaMA-based models currently and worry about compatibility on certain kernel builds.
[05:19] Miguel: We verify model variants on our runtime; during onboarding we can validate your exact model artifacts. Sometimes quantization changes hallucination characteristics, so we do a quick eval set. We'll coordinate model onboarding with your ML team.
[05:35] Rina: Who are other vendors we've been comparing? Marcus, you had a note?
[05:39] Marcus: We looked at Anthropic's endpoint for safety controls, OpenAI for ease of use, and a smaller onprem vendor AuroraAI for private hosting. Main differentiator for Redwood is the observability and the routing/fallback policies.
[05:56] Sofia: Good notes. We'll call out where we differ on observability, rollout controls, and cost levers.
[06:03] [00:06:03] Noah: On contract length — if we do a 12-month commit, what's the uplift flexibility? Can we add regions mid-term?
[06:12] Caroline: Yes, we support mid-term region adds. We usually treat additional regions as add-ons with a short provisioning lead time; pricing can be pro-rated for the remainder of the term.
[06:24] Rina: For the EU pilot we'd like a small private cluster ~2 nodes for canary, then scale to 10 nodes over 6 months. Is that feasible?
[06:33] Miguel: Absolutely — that fits our stepped-provisioning approach. We'll propose an autoscale headroom and a rolling activation so you don't pay for fully provisioned capacity immediately.
[06:42] Marcus: Any network prerequisites? We need to know firewall rules, peering, and whitelisted IP blocks.
[06:49] Miguel: We'll provide a VPC onboarding checklist: CIDR ranges, allowed egress, peering steps, health check endpoints, and VPN/Direct Connect options.
[06:59] Rina: Regarding audit logs — how long are request-level logs retained? We need 1 year for a specific workflow.
[07:05] Caroline: Default retention is 90 days for request logs, but we have add-on retention for 1+ years for compliance customers — we'll include the options and costs.
[07:15] [00:07:15] Dana: On the perf POC — can we run a synthetic with our data distribution? If we can't share PII, we can obfuscate tokens.
[07:24] Miguel: Yes, we can run synthetic traces. We also support an on-site benchmarking harness you can run in your environment to mirror network conditions. For sensitive data, we recommend redaction or synthetic equivalents.
[07:36] Noah: Legal will ask for indemnities and data handling clauses. Do you have a standard enterprise exhibit we can start from?
[07:43] Caroline: We'll attach a standard enterprise exhibit and can incorporate additional legal requirements; we usually iterate with procurement within two weeks.
[07:50] Rina: Ok good. For the pricing sketches, can you show the break-even point where Dedicated becomes cheaper than Hosted given our QPS?
[07:58] Sofia: Yep — that's one of the core comparisons we'll show: cost per 1k tokens at your median and peak patterns, and the break-even QPS.
[08:06] [00:08:06] Marcus: Slight aside — last month we saw a p99 outlier where latency hit 1.8s, not sure why. Can Redwood route to a fallback model or lower-latency smaller model automatically?
[08:17] Miguel: We support automated fallback policies and model variants. For example, we can route to a faster quantized variant when the primary pool is saturated. That's part of the graceful degradation features.
[08:29] Rina: Perfect. That might save costs vs overprovisioning.
[08:33] Sofia: Exactly — it's a cost and reliability lever we usually highlight.
[08:36] [00:08:36] Noah: Any blockers to commit timeline? We want a signed contract by mid-October and production activation in November for EU VPC.
[08:45] Caroline: If legal and SOC2 review go quickly and procurement returns redlines by Oct 6, then yes mid-October signing is feasible. The bottleneck is whether you want HSM — that adds lead time.
[08:57] Dana: We'll try to avoid HSM initially; cloud KMS with bring-your-own-key is acceptable for the pilot.
[09:05] Miguel: Cool — that shortens the path. We'll include KMS integration steps and checklist.
[09:11] Rina: For the POC — what's the minimal commitment? Can we do a 2-week pilot with limited throughput?
[09:17] Sofia: Yes — we'll propose a 2-week POC scope: targeted routes, synthetic load, success criteria (p95 under X ms, cost delta under Y%), and a go/no-go decision at the end.
[09:29] Marcus: Success criteria: p95 < 250ms for assist flows at 90th percentile traffic, and token cost delta under 30% vs hosted baseline.
[09:39] Miguel: We'll reflect that in the POC plan.
[09:42] [00:09:42] Rina: I also want to understand support during the pilot — is there an on-call SE?
[09:47] Caroline: We'll assign a named SE and provide escalation paths; for pilots we usually include a couple of office hours and a Slack channel.
[09:55] Noah: On billing — do you offer net-30?
[09:58] Caroline: Standard is net-30 for enterprise; we can align with your procurement if needed.
[10:04] Rina: Anything else we should consider?
[10:07] Sofia: One more thing — if you plan to add multiple regions later, consider setting up a cross-region failover policy and a single billing seat to simplify operations. We'll show recommended routing policies in the proposal.
[10:19] Marcus: Sounds good.
[10:21] [00:10:21] (brief hold)
[10:45] Miguel: Quick technical note — regarding model quantization, we'll run a short eval with your eval set to check quality regressions. If we see >2% regression on your core metrics we'll surface that before rolling out.
[10:58] Dana: Good — quality is the blocker for us.
[11:01] Rina: Okay let's recap then.
[11:03] Sofia: Recap: Redwood to send three pricing options and contract sketches by Oct 3; Caroline to share SOC2 + VPC checklist by Oct 1; Miguel to draft POC plan for a 2-week perf check by Oct 7; GlimmerOps (Dana/Marcus/Noah) to confirm procurement dates and whether HSM needed by Oct 2.
[11:23] Noah: We'll try to hit those dates.
[11:26] Rina: Great. Any final questions?
[11:29] Marcus: Minor — are there any additional fees for audit log export?
[11:33] Caroline: Export to your log storage can be configured; prolonged retention or push to third-party archival has an add-on cost, we'll include numbers.
[11:41] Sofia: Thanks all — we'll follow up with an email with the next steps and links.
[11:46] Dana: Thanks.
[11:48] [00:11:48] End meeting.
